title: How do you balance enjoyment of films with your daily life (if it is not related to your job)?

commenti.body:
My little brother has been obsessed with movies since we were little children, and he just finished and released his debut feature film, which premiered at the Sydney Film Festival and went on to a two week theatrical run nationally here in Australia.


He got his start by making little films with our parents video camera. You have the advantage of living in a time where your mobile phone can probably shoot 4k, and good, free editing software is widely accessible. 


It's the same way pretty much every aspiring film maker starts. 


So make a bunch of stuff. Its probably not going to be very good at first, that's okay. You'll get a taste for whether or not you actually enjoy making things, or if you're happy just to view them. Then if you find you do like it, just keep learning as much as you can about all aspects of production.


Worst case scenario, you'll have a fun hobby.
[removed]

Kudos to your brother for sticking with it. 

Sound advice.

It was never going to be any other way for him. He's one of those people who absolutely knew what he wanted to do it and has been relentlessly pursuing it his whole life. He's just about to head to head off to Europe to try and find distribution for his film over there!

Could always make short films and put them on youtube or something. All i'm saying is if its something you really want to do you should pursue it and don't expect it to be great or perfect or a blockbuster hit. It doesn't have to be any of those things and nobody gets good at anything that fast. Lots of practice. And then maybe one day you think you are ready you could try to get a scholarship or like i think kevin smith just put it all on credit cards for Clerks. But that was also a huge gamble.
What’s the film, and is there distribution online? I’m from NZ and love to support films from our side of the world. Would def buy an online copy or something!

I’m in a similar but not identical spot. I’m 19, so I’m already a year into Uni, and it’s relatively affordable where I’m from so I’m pretty lucky to be able to go to film school. I also had high grades in most other areas and people expected me to go into politics or economics. I just had to do what I love, but I’m fortunate to have the opportunity to do so.

I know it’s not the most stable career path but remember going to film school doesn’t just give the option of director. There are many roles on and off set that are benefitted by a film degree, and depending on where you’re from the course can be super helpful for learning how to translate your film love into film creation. 

Listen to the advice of everyone else too about just starting on short films now. I’ve had great times hanging out with friends and just seeing what we could make, and I’m pretty proud whenever I finish a project that I’ve worked hard to make. It doesn’t take a lot and doesn’t need to be big or impressive, just a start, a path for creative fulfilment, and a way to learn by doing.

You can 100% dedicate your life to filmmaking. And if that doesn’t work out, then you can dedicate your life to something else. Sounds like you’ve got no one depending on you but yourself, so the cost of “failure” is pretty low, and at your age you have plenty of time to change careers multiple times. Instead of film school, move to LA and try to get an entry level job at anywhere even remotely associated with the industry (or get a bs job to pay the bills while you make shorts and learn the craft). Go for it!

If you want to have a life that consistently integrates pragmatic career choices with creative passions, you are very unlikely to be able to plan it out in advance at the age of 16. Start exploring your interests seriously now while keeping your options open. If you have really high grades, go to the best university you can, study what interests you (without presuming a career track), and meet people who share your interests. When you're done, you will almost certainly have a better perspective on where you want to go, and better way to get there.

In the meantime, just start making some short films right now. You don't need anything special—you could start with an iPhone—and you don't need to label it a hobby or a career. If you're passionate about making films, that's not what really matters, right? Just get into a project!

Oh that's awesome, thanks! His film is called The Big Dog ([IMDb](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt27881639/))  


I am 99% sure that New Zealand was also in the distribution region for Apple TV and Amazon, so you should be able to rent/purchase it from either of those. I hope you enjoy it!
[removed]

Working with film does not have to mean making the films. You can also go into academia with Cinema Studies where you will discuss how we make sense of all of these moving images around us, and use that knowledge to work in a film related field, such as distribution, projection environments (i.e. cinemas), film politics, film archives, film festivals, working with film in corporate contexts, et cetera. And of course you can always do a PHD in Cinema Studies and devout your time to researching those obscure low budget films that you are talking about :) personally Im currently doing a masters in the field and having the opportunity to discuss my favourite films in my essays is a lot of fun.
[removed]

Film appreciation is a lovely hobby. I went to The Boston Conservatory. No one made it there in anything noteworthy regarding tv or film, or Broadway. Our biggest actress had her biggest film role in The House Bunny. It’s not enough to go to conservatory. 

However, if you can create a beautiful scene on your expensive phone camera with good actors, you’ve got a shot at winning a scholarship at UNCSA. On a scholarship it’s very affordable if you’re in-state. I have extensive acting studies. And I’ve always wanted to play Paul Lynde. And I’m a comedy writer. Well anyway, it’s always ok to submit an application. You can decide after your audition.
This looks awesome,  congrats to your brother! I hope we'll manage to watch it in Europe one day, fingers crossed.
Thanks! I hope so too!
[removed]
Maybe a dumb question, but what do you mean by 'film politics'?
Sweet, I’m on vacation but when I get back I’ll check it out!

Maybe not the term used in other langauges and a bad translation from me but I mean how film supported by politics, via grants et cetera, is supposed to be carried out and decided around. Like, for who are the films that are getting grants and how is film spread in society, both practically as well as an idea. But this might not be relevant in certain countries. For some countries it is more or less impossible to produce films without state grants.
I get now and what you were going for. You mean something like being on the socioeconomic side of cinema. Thanks for elaborating.
Thanks for asking!
